page: UpCloud HIMEM-2xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance within the High Memory family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 100 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates constrained performance across compute and memory subsystems. The shared CPU allocation model results in poor stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, register in the weak category (bottom 25%). Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores fall within the bottom 25%. While the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded bzip3 decompression reach average levels (middle 50%), multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput remain poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, but it presents significant performance tradeoffs due to its shared CPU resources and weak memory bandwidth. It is not suited for compute-intensive tasks, high-throughput web serving, or large-scale database operations. Instead, the hardware profile is appropriate for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic background utilities, development environments, or small-scale applications with low CPU utilization.
